model.name: Financial Transaction / Journal Entry
model.purpose: Represent the recorded accounting event that posts a balanced set of debit and credit lines to financial accounts, with identity, control, audit evidence and interchange independent of ledger product or file format.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the atomic posting and the balanced journal entry that groups postings: identifiers, classification, header and line composition, debit-credit balancing, amounts and currencies, recognition and measurement basis, posting lifecycle, authorization, period cutoff, provenance, supporting evidence, retention and mappings to ledger and cash-reporting standards. It does not own account masters, payment instructions, party masters, commercial invoices or financial-statement roll-ups.
in_scope: Balanced journal entries composed of a header and two or more posting lines
Atomic account postings with debit or credit indicator, amount, account reference and narrative
Bank-booked cash entries reported by an account servicer that must be reconciled into a sub-ledger or general ledger
Lifecycle states including unposted or draft, posted, reversed, recurring, adjusting, closing, consolidating and other period-end or top-side adjustments
Multi-currency amounts, exchange-rate evidence and measurement basis of the recognised amounts
Controls over initiating, authorizing, recording and processing entries, including manual versus automated origin
Event times distinct from ingestion times, fiscal-period assignment and closed-period constraints
Audit-trail provenance, supporting documents, population completeness and interchange with XBRL GL and ISO 20022 cash reporting
out_of_scope: Financial account, chart of accounts and ledger-master data owned by WM-ECO-015
Payment initiation, clearing, settlement and cash-transfer instructions owned by WM-ECO-009 except as an originating reference
Legal-entity, party, instrument, product and invoice masters except as references on a posting
Financial statements, trial balances and XBRL financial-reporting facts as aggregated outputs
Budgets, forecasts, commitments and other non-posted management measures
FIBO securities and derivatives trade workflows, which use the word transaction for market processes rather than ledger postings
Tax-return forms and statutory reports except as consumers of exported journal populations

boundary_notes.distinction: An account is the persistent ledger container and classification of claims on resources; this model is the time-stamped posting event that changes account balances. Account identifiers are referenced, not redefined.

A payment is an instruction or transfer of funds between parties. A journal entry is the accounting recognition of that or another economic event. One payment may generate several postings; many journal entries have no payment origin.

FIBO BP models securities issuance and trade process flows and their temporal semantics. That market-side transaction is not the same object as a double-entry journal posting, even when both are called financial transactions.

Invoices, receipts and contracts are evidential source documents that may trigger postings. They are not the journal entry. XBRL GL and PCAOB both treat documents as support for entries, not as the entry itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Financial statements and XBRL FR reports
boundary_notes.distinction: Statements and reporting taxonomies aggregate and present recognised elements. XBRL GL retains transactional detail so those aggregates can be drilled back to journal lines; this model stops at the posting, not the statement.

sources.title: XBRL Global Ledger Taxonomy Framework 2015
sources.relevance: Normative modular taxonomy for journal entries, ledgers, multicurrency, Saxonic journal tagging and tax-audit fields, with accountingEntries, modules COR BUS MUC USK TAF SRCD.

sources.title: XBRL Global Ledger: Transactional Reporting
sources.relevance: Defines XBRL GL as the system-independent record of original ledger detail, journal entries and drill-down from summary reports, including audit, consolidation and transfer use.

sources.title: Audit Focus: Journal Entries
sources.relevance: Authoritative staff reminder of journal-entry testing: controls over initiate-authorize-record-process, completeness of the population, manual versus automated origin, post-closing and fraudulent-entry characteristics.

sources.title: AS 2401: Consideration of Fraud in a Financial Statement Audit
sources.version_or_date: current PCAOB auditing standard as published 2026-08-25
sources.relevance: Requires examination of journal entries and other adjustments for management override, including nonstandard, consolidating and reclassification adjustments not always in formal journal entries.

sources.title: AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements
sources.version_or_date: current PCAOB auditing standard as published 2026-08-25
sources.relevance: Requires controls over journal entries and period-end adjustments, significant unusual transactions that result in late or unusual journal entries, and procedures to initiate, authorize, record and process entries in the general ledger.

sources.title: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
sources.version_or_date: revised March 2018; company effective date 1 January 2020
sources.relevance: Defines recognition and derecognition of assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses, measurement bases, reporting period and qualitative characteristics that a posting must faithfully represent.

sources.title: Catalogue of messages
sources.relevance: Official inventory of approved ISO 20022 message definitions, including cash-management and account-reporting messages used to report booked cash transactions.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Bank Transaction Codes - External Code Sets
sources.relevance: Harmonised bank transaction codes for bank-to-customer cash account reporting so the account owner can reconcile cash movements to sub-ledgers and processing systems.

sources.title: ISO 4217 — Currency codes
sources.relevance: Alphabetic and numeric currency codes and minor-unit exponents required to express posting amounts without ambiguity.

sources.title: Financial Industry Business Ontology (FIBO) repository
sources.relevance: Formal OWL vocabulary for financial contracts and process flows; BP domain transaction semantics are an adjacent meaning of financial transaction that must not be collapsed into a ledger posting.

sources.title: ISO 20022 Message Definitions
sources.relevance: Machine-readable message inventory and schemas for ISO 20022, including account management and other financial-message families that carry booked amounts and references.

sources.title: Transactional Reporting (Global Ledger)
sources.relevance: States that XBRL GL represents chart of accounts, journal entries and historical transactions without requiring a standardised chart of accounts.

sources.title: ISO 20022 MDR Part 1 BankToCustomer Cash Management
sources.relevance: Message definition report for bank-to-customer cash management, including BankToCustomerStatement camt.053, designed to report cash transactions between an account servicer and its customers.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a journal entry or posting is uniquely identified, typed and placed in a reporting entity, ledger book and source journal.
bundles.rationale: Agents cannot operate postings without a master-system identifier, a type that distinguishes standard, adjusting and automated entries, and the reporting-entity and book context required by both XBRL GL entityInformation and IFRS reporting-entity concepts.

layers.name: Identifiers and correlation keys
layers.description: Master-system numbers, governed global references and Dimension-assigned identifiers for the entry and its lines.

findings.name: Master and correlating identifiers
findings.description: A posting is identified first by the identifier assigned by the posting ledger or account servicer, then by any governed global reference used for reconciliation, then by a Dimension UUID or ULID. Dates are not identifiers.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier did the posting ledger or account servicer assign to this journal entry or booked entry?
Which governed end-to-end or instruction identifiers, if any, correlate this posting to a payment, statement entry or external transaction?
What UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign when no master-system or governed global identifier is reusable as the canonical key?
How are posting-line identifiers formed so they remain unique under reversal, restatement and multi-book copies?

data_elements.name: Journal entry number
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the posting ledger or ERP document numbering scheme.

data_elements.name: Account servicer reference
data_elements.description: Servicer-assigned reference for a booked cash entry used in bank-to-customer reporting and reconciliation.

data_elements.name: Dimension identifier
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when the master identifier is absent, unstable or not globally unique.

data_elements.name: End-to-end correlation identifier
data_elements.description: Optional governed identifier linking the posting to a payment or other originating instruction.

artifacts.name: Numbered journal voucher
artifacts.description: System of record artefact carrying the journal entry number, lines and control totals as issued by the posting ledger.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the ledger document number as the artefact serial; do not derive identity from posting date.

layers.name: Type, origin and reporting context
layers.description: Classification of the entry and the reporting entity, book and source journal in which it is recorded.

findings.name: Entry type and origin class
findings.description: Entries must be classified by purpose (standard, adjusting, reversing, recurring, closing, consolidating, reclassification, statistical or memo) and by origin (manual, automated, subsidiary-ledger generated, bank-statement imported, top-side).

questions.text: What is the governed type of this journal entry or adjustment, including whether it is standard, adjusting, reversing, recurring, closing, consolidating or a reclassification?
Was the entry initiated manually, generated automatically from a subledger or bank feed, or processed as a top-side adjustment outside the normal course of business?
Which source journal or specialised ledger (general, sales, cash, payroll, tax, memo) originated the entry?

data_elements.name: Entry type code
data_elements.description: Code for the accounting purpose of the entry.

data_elements.name: Origin class
data_elements.description: Manual, automated, imported, or top-side origin used in fraud-risk selection.

data_elements.name: Source journal identifier
data_elements.description: XBRL GL sourceJournalID or equivalent specialised-journal code.

artifacts.name: Entry type catalogue
artifacts.description: Governed list of entry types and origin classes used by the Dimension, mapped to XBRL GL and PCAOB testing classes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by catalogue IRI plus type code, not by effective date.

findings.name: Reporting entity, book and ownership
findings.description: Each posting belongs to a reporting entity and a named book or ledger view (statutory, management, tax or other). Ownership of the books sits with the reporting entity; the ledger operator or account servicer maintains the record.

questions.text: Which reporting entity owns the books in which this entry is recognised, and under which identifier scheme is that entity named?
Which accounting book, ledger view or parallel set of books (statutory, IFRS, local GAAP, tax, management) received the posting?
Who operates the system of record for this posting: the reporting entity, an outsourced accountant, or an account servicer?
In which tax or reporting jurisdiction are these books kept for audit-file and retention purposes?

data_elements.name: Reporting entity identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the entity that prepares the financial statements or tax file containing the posting.

data_elements.name: Book code
data_elements.description: Named set of books or ledger view to which the entry is posted.

data_elements.name: GAAP or framework
data_elements.description: Financial-reporting framework governing recognition in this book.

artifacts.name: Entity information block
artifacts.description: XBRL GL entityInformation or equivalent header naming the reporting organisation, book and period of the instance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by reporting-entity identifier plus book code.

bundles.name: Composition and balancing
bundles.description: Header-and-line structure of a journal entry, the accounts it posts to, and the debit-equals-credit invariant.
bundles.rationale: XBRL GL models entryHeader containing entryDetail lines with account and debitCreditCode. PCAOB treats the journal entry as the unit of recording in the general ledger. Balancing is the operating constraint that makes the posting an accounting event rather than a single-sided memo.

layers.name: Header and posting lines
layers.description: The journal header and the atomic posting lines that reference accounts and carry debit or credit amounts.

findings.name: Journal entry header
findings.description: The header groups lines that must balance together, carries the entry number, preparer, source journal, narrative and document references, and is the unit reversed or adjusted as a whole unless a partial reversal is explicitly recorded.

questions.text: What header narrative, document number, source journal and preparer attributes describe this journal entry as a whole?
How many posting lines belong to this header, and which line identifiers constitute the complete set?
Which source documents (invoice, bank statement, contract, spreadsheet) are referenced from the header as the economic origin of the entry?
Is the header a complete balanced set, a proposed or parked set, or an incomplete import batch that must not yet post?

data_elements.name: Entry narrative
data_elements.description: Header-level explanation of the economic event.

data_elements.name: Source document number
data_elements.description: External or internal document number associated with the header.

data_elements.name: Entered by
data_elements.description: User or system that captured the header, corresponding to XBRL GL enteredBy.

data_elements.name: Line identifier list
data_elements.description: Ordered collection of posting-line identifiers owned by the header.

artifacts.name: Journal header record
artifacts.description: Header artefact grouping lines, narrative and control totals before or after posting.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Header identity is the journal entry number in the issuing ledger, qualified by company and book, not by date.

findings.name: Atomic posting line
findings.description: Each line posts one amount to one account (with optional sub-account dimensions) as a debit or credit. The line is the atomic transfer against WM-ECO-015 accounts.

questions.text: Which financial account and optional sub-account dimensions receive this posting line?
Is the line a debit or a credit, and is that fact stored as a code rather than a signed amount?
What line narrative and cost objects, divisions or other analytical dimensions accompany the account posting?
If the line originated from bank reporting, what bank transaction code domain, family and sub-family classify the cash movement?

data_elements.name: Account identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the WM-ECO-015 account posted.

data_elements.name: Debit or credit code
data_elements.description: Indicator that the line is a debit or a credit; when present the amount should not be signed.

data_elements.name: Line amount
data_elements.description: Unsigned monetary amount of the line in the line currency.

data_elements.name: Bank transaction code
data_elements.description: ISO 20022 bank transaction code used to reconcile a cash movement to a sub-ledger.

data_elements.name: Analytical dimensions
data_elements.description: Optional cost objects and organisational splits carried on the line.

artifacts.name: Posting line record
artifacts.description: Atomic line artefact with account, debit-credit code, amount and optional bank transaction code.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Line identity is parent journal identifier plus stable line number or line UUID.

layers.name: Balancing rules
layers.description: Constraints that make a set of lines a valid journal entry.

findings.name: Debit-credit balance and posting unit
findings.description: For a double-entry journal, the sum of debits must equal the sum of credits in the balancing currency of the header. Single-sided bank statement entries are not themselves balanced journals; they become journals only when counterpart lines are posted. Out-of-balance intercompany and top-side packs are exception states, not the default.

questions.text: Do the header's debit totals equal its credit totals in the balancing currency, and what is the residual if they do not?
Is this object a single-sided bank-booked entry still awaiting counterpart posting, or a complete journal that already balances?
What exception, intercompany lag or currency rounding rule is allowed to leave a residual, and who must clear it?

data_elements.name: Debit total
data_elements.description: Sum of debit line amounts in the balancing currency.

data_elements.name: Credit total
data_elements.description: Sum of credit line amounts in the balancing currency.

data_elements.name: Is balanced
data_elements.description: Whether debit total equals credit total within the governed tolerance.

data_elements.name: Balancing currency
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 currency in which the header is required to balance.

artifacts.name: Balance control total
artifacts.description: Control-total record proving debit and credit equality at post time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by journal entry number plus validation run identifier.

bundles.name: Measurement and recognition
bundles.description: Monetary amounts, currencies, exchange rates and the recognition or derecognition basis that justifies posting an element.
bundles.rationale: ISO 4217 is required to name currencies. XBRL GL MUC supplies multicurrency fields. The IFRS Conceptual Framework supplies recognition, derecognition and measurement bases that distinguish a booked cash movement from a recognised accounting element.

layers.name: Amounts and currency
layers.description: Quantities, currencies, minor units and foreign-exchange conversion used on lines and headers.

findings.name: Monetary amount, currency and FX
findings.description: Each amount is a quantity in an ISO 4217 currency with known minor-unit exponent. Functional, transaction and reporting currencies may differ; rates and rate sources must be recorded when conversion occurs.

questions.text: What unsigned amount and ISO 4217 currency, including minor-unit exponent, apply to each posting line?
If the line currency differs from the functional or balancing currency, what rate, rate type, rate source and conversion time were used?
Which currencies play the transaction, functional and presentation roles for this entry?
Is this posting an original transaction, a foreign-currency revaluation, or a translation adjustment?

data_elements.name: Amount
data_elements.description: Unsigned decimal monetary quantity.

data_elements.name: Currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code.

data_elements.name: Foreign exchange rate
data_elements.description: Conversion rate applied when line currency differs from functional or balancing currency.

data_elements.name: Functional currency amount
data_elements.description: Amount expressed in the reporting entity's functional currency.

artifacts.name: FX rate evidence
artifacts.description: Rate source extract or system rate table row used to convert the posting.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by rate source, currency pair, rate type and conversion timestamp, not by journal date alone.

layers.name: Recognition and measurement basis
layers.description: Whether the posting recognises or derecognises an IFRS (or other framework) element and on which measurement basis.

findings.name: Recognition, derecognition and measurement basis
findings.description: A posting should state which elements (asset, liability, equity, income, expense) it recognises or derecognises and the measurement basis (historical cost, current value or other framework basis). Cash booking on a bank statement does not by itself establish IFRS recognition.

questions.text: Which financial-statement elements does this entry recognise or derecognise, and is recognition justified by the applicable framework?
On which measurement basis are the posted amounts stated, and does that basis differ from the cash amount booked by the account servicer?
Which accounting policy or materiality judgement authorised this recognition when no specific standard line-item rule applies?

data_elements.name: Elements affected
data_elements.description: Asset, liability, equity, income or expense flags for the lines.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis
data_elements.description: Historical cost, current value or other basis used for the posted amount.

data_elements.name: Recognition or derecognition
data_elements.description: Whether the entry adds or removes a recognised element.

artifacts.name: Recognition policy memo
artifacts.description: Policy or judgement artefact cited when the posting depends on Conceptual Framework or IAS 8-style policy choice.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by policy IRI or memo identifier, not by the period date.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, control and authority
bundles.description: States of a journal entry, permitted transitions, who may initiate and authorize, and closed-period exceptions.
bundles.rationale: PCAOB AS 2401 and AS 2201 require understanding of controls over initiating, authorizing, recording and processing journal entries, including period-end, late, unusual and nonstandard adjustments and the risk of management override.

layers.name: Posting states and rare transitions
layers.description: Draft through posted, reversed, restated and other exceptional states.

findings.name: Lifecycle state of the entry
findings.description: Typical states include proposed or parked, rejected, posted, period-locked, reversed and restated. Posted entries are not silently overwritten. Automated and manual paths share the same state machine because override risk is not limited to manual entries.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle state of the journal entry, and which timestamps mark each completed transition?
Which role is allowed to move this entry from its current state to each permitted next state?
If the entry is posted, is in-place update forbidden so that any correction must create a reversing or restating entry?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Current state of the entry in the posting state machine.

data_elements.name: Posted immutability flag
data_elements.description: Whether the posted record is frozen against silent update.

data_elements.name: State history
data_elements.description: Sequence of states with actors and times.

artifacts.name: State transition log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of lifecycle transitions for the journal entry.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each transition has its own event identifier; the journal number is the parent, not the transition id.

findings.name: Reversals, corrections and period-end adjustments
findings.description: Rare but required cases include auto-reversing accruals, prior-period corrections, consolidating and reclassification adjustments, late or unusual entries, and top-side adjustments that may not appear as formal journal entries in the general ledger.

questions.text: Is this entry a reversal, a correcting entry, a prior-period restatement, or an auto-reversing accrual, and which original entry does it supersede?
Is this adjustment a consolidating, combination, reclassification or other top-side item that is not reflected as a formal journal entry in the general ledger?
Was the entry recorded at period end or post-close, to seldom-used accounts, by an unusual preparer, or with round-number or unexplained characteristics?

data_elements.name: Adjustment class
data_elements.description: Reversal, correction, auto-reversing accrual, restatement, consolidation, reclassification or top-side.

data_elements.name: Original entry identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the entry being reversed or corrected.

data_elements.name: Top-side flag
data_elements.description: Whether the adjustment is outside formal general-ledger journal entries.

data_elements.name: Post-close flag
data_elements.description: Whether the entry was recorded after books were closed.

artifacts.name: Reversal or adjusting voucher
artifacts.description: Document that reverses or adjusts a prior posted entry, including link to the original.
artifacts.identity_strategy: New journal number for the reversing or adjusting document; original number stored as a reference, never reused as the identity of the reversal.

layers.name: Authorization, access and period lock
layers.description: Who may initiate, authorize, record and process entries, and how closed periods are enforced.

findings.name: Initiate, authorize, record and process
findings.description: Controls must cover initiation, authorization, recording and processing of both automated and manual journal entries in the general ledger, subsidiary ledgers and other IT systems. Segregation of duties and dual control are expected except where a documented compensating control exists.

questions.text: Who initiated this entry and who authorized it, and are those persons different under the segregation-of-duties rule?
Through which IT systems or interfaces was the entry recorded and processed, including subledger feeds?
Which roles may read the entry or its supporting evidence, and which fields are restricted as personal or commercially sensitive?
Was any control overridden, and what management or system override evidence exists?

data_elements.name: Initiator identifier
data_elements.description: Person or system that initiated the entry.

data_elements.name: Authorizer identifier
data_elements.description: Person or system that authorized posting.

data_elements.name: Segregation of duties satisfied
data_elements.description: Whether initiator and authorizer are distinct as required.

data_elements.name: Control override flag
data_elements.description: Whether a control was overridden for this entry.

artifacts.name: Authorization record
artifacts.description: Approval artefact or system workflow step proving authorization before post.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by authorization event identifier linked to the journal number.

findings.name: Period lock, closed-book posting and access exceptions
findings.description: Posted activity must be assigned to an open fiscal period. Posting to a closed period requires an explicit exception, typically limited to authorized adjusting entries. Access to create or alter entries is denied by default.

questions.text: Is the target fiscal period open for this book, and if closed what exception grant allows this posting?
What is the default access rule for creating or changing entries in this book, and which scoped exceptions apply?
Do any lines carry personal data (for example payroll names) that require a stricter access scope than the header?

data_elements.name: Period status
data_elements.description: Open, closing, closed or locked status of the target period.

data_elements.name: Closed-period exception grant
data_elements.description: Identifier of the grant that allows posting into a closed period.

data_elements.name: Contains personal data
data_elements.description: Whether posting lines include personal data requiring restricted access.

artifacts.name: Period lock and exception log
artifacts.description: Record of period open, close and exception grants for the book.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by book plus period identifier plus lock-event identifier.

bundles.name: Time and fiscal period
bundles.description: Event times versus observation times, and assignment of the posting to a reporting period.
bundles.rationale: IFRS financial statements are prepared for a specified period. PCAOB testing depends on when entries were recorded, especially at period end. ISO 20022 cash reporting distinguishes booking date and value date. XBRL GL distinguishes entered date from other operational dates.

layers.name: Event and observation times
layers.description: Document, posting, value, booking and entry-capture times, kept distinct from ingestion time.

findings.name: Accounting event timestamps
findings.description: A posting may have several event times: economic document date, ledger posting date, cash value date and bank booking date. These are event times. The time the Dimension ingested the record is observation time and must not replace event time. All values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

questions.text: What are the document, posting, value and booking date-times of this event, each with seconds and an explicit offset or Z?
When was this record observed or ingested by the Dimension, and does that time differ from the accounting event time?
When was the entry captured (entered) versus when was it posted to the ledger, and who performed each act?

data_elements.name: Document time
data_elements.description: Economic or source-document date-time of the event.

data_elements.name: Posting time
data_elements.description: Date-time the ledger recognised the entry.

data_elements.name: Value time
data_elements.description: Cash value date-time when relevant to bank or treasury postings.

data_elements.name: Booking time
data_elements.description: Account-servicer booking date-time of a cash entry.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Observation time when the Dimension received the record.

artifacts.name: Timestamp set
artifacts.description: Recorded set of event and ingestion timestamps for the posting.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Timestamps are attributes of the journal or entry identifier; a date is never used as the identifier.

layers.name: Fiscal period and cutoff
layers.description: Assignment of the posting to a reporting period and cutoff judgements.

findings.name: Fiscal period assignment and cutoff
findings.description: Each recognised posting is assigned to a reporting period of the reporting entity. Cutoff errors (posting in the wrong period) are a primary completeness and occurrence risk. Comparative information belongs to other periods, not to this event.

questions.text: To which fiscal period and reporting year is this posting assigned, and which calendar produces that period?
Does the economic event belong in this period under the entity's cutoff policy, or should it be accrued or reversed into another period?
Are the financial statements that will consume this posting prepared on a going-concern basis for the specified period?

data_elements.name: Fiscal period identifier
data_elements.description: Period code to which the posting is assigned.

data_elements.name: Period start
data_elements.description: Start of the reporting period.

data_elements.name: Period end
data_elements.description: End of the reporting period.

artifacts.name: Period assignment record
artifacts.description: Binding of the journal to a named fiscal period of the reporting entity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Period identity is the calendar period code, not the posting date string.

bundles.name: Provenance, evidence, quality and retention
bundles.description: Who created the record, what supports it, whether the population is complete, and how long it must be kept.
bundles.rationale: PCAOB requires testing accuracy and completeness of the journal-entry population and examining supporting evidence, not inquiry alone. XBRL GL exists so transactional detail is retained rather than lost in summary reports. TAF fields exist for tax audit export.

layers.name: Provenance and supporting evidence
layers.description: Lineage from source system to posted record, plus documentary evidence.

findings.name: Provenance and system lineage
findings.description: Each posting should record creating system, extract or message identifier, actors, and hashes or control totals used to prove the record was not altered after post.

questions.text: From which source system, message or extract did this posting originate, and what identifiers chain it back to that source?
What integrity hash, electronic signature or control total attests that the posted record is unaltered?
Which mappings or transformations were applied between the source message and the posted journal, and who owns those mappings?

data_elements.name: Source system
data_elements.description: System that originated the posting or extract.

data_elements.name: Content hash
data_elements.description: Integrity digest of the canonical posted record.

data_elements.name: Lineage chain
data_elements.description: Ordered references from source message to posted journal.

artifacts.name: Provenance record
artifacts.description: Lineage and integrity metadata bound to the posted entry.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by provenance-event identifier linked to the master journal identifier.

findings.name: Supporting documents and evidence quality
findings.description: Selected entries must be corroborated by supporting evidence. Inquiry alone is insufficient. Missing explanation, missing account numbers, or absent documentation are quality defects and fraud-risk indicators.

questions.text: What supporting documents corroborate this entry, and do they corroborate or contradict the posting?
Is the evidence sufficiently precise and complete for audit or tax-file use, including account numbers and explanations?
Who holds the original evidence, and is it immutable for the retention period?

data_elements.name: Evidence document identifiers
data_elements.description: References to invoices, statements, contracts or worksheets that support the posting.

data_elements.name: Corroboration result
data_elements.description: Whether evidence corroborates, is missing, or contradicts the posting.

data_elements.name: Has explanation
data_elements.description: Whether the entry carries a substantive narrative.

artifacts.name: Supporting source document
artifacts.description: Invoice, bank statement, contract or other document examined as evidence of the posting.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the source-document master identifier; do not use the journal date as the document id.

layers.name: Population completeness, fraud testing and retention
layers.description: Completeness of the journal population, fraud-oriented selection, and retention or deletion constraints.

findings.name: Population completeness and fraud-oriented selection
findings.description: The list of journal entries produced by the company must be tested for accuracy and completeness before items are selected. Selection considers fraud-risk characteristics: seldom-used accounts, unusual preparers, period-end or post-close timing, missing account numbers, round numbers, and items processed outside the normal course of business. Automated entries remain in scope.

questions.text: Was the journal-entry population tested for accuracy and completeness, including entries imported into analysis tools?
Which fraud-risk criteria selected this entry for testing, and what rationale exists if a matching entry was excluded?
What did individuals involved in processing journal entries say about inappropriate or unusual activity, and is that inquiry documented?

data_elements.name: Population count
data_elements.description: Count of journal entries in the tested population.

data_elements.name: Fraud criteria matched
data_elements.description: List of AS 2401.61-style characteristics that this entry meets.

data_elements.name: Exclusion rationale
data_elements.description: Documented reason for not testing an entry that met fraud criteria.

artifacts.name: Journal population extract
artifacts.description: Complete extract of journal entries from which audit or analytics samples are drawn, with control totals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by extract run identifier plus entity and period; the extract is not identified by a calendar date string alone.

findings.name: Retention, deletion and legal hold
findings.description: Posted journals and supporting evidence are retained for financial-reporting, audit and tax-audit purposes. XBRL GL TAF exists to export reliable detail to tax agencies. Silent deletion of posted entries is not a normal operation; legal holds override ordinary disposal.

questions.text: What retention period and legal basis apply to this posted entry and its evidence in the relevant jurisdiction?
Is the entry under legal hold, tax audit or other freeze that forbids deletion or alteration?
If the entry is unposted draft, may it be discarded, and if posted, is only a reversing entry allowed rather than physical delete?

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Governed duration or explicit disposal eligibility time.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Whether disposal is frozen.

data_elements.name: Posted physical delete forbidden
data_elements.description: Whether physical deletion of a posted entry is prohibited.

artifacts.name: Retention and hold record
artifacts.description: Policy instance or legal-hold artefact covering the journal and its evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by hold or schedule identifier linked to the journal master identifier.

bundles.name: Interoperability and alignments
bundles.description: Mappings to XBRL GL, ISO 20022 cash reporting and adjacent ontologies, including known semantic conflicts.
bundles.rationale: Agents must project this format-neutral model onto XBRL GL instances and ISO 20022 bank-to-customer cash messages without treating those projections as the semantics, and without equating FIBO market transactions or summary XBRL FR facts with journal entries.

layers.name: Standard mappings
layers.description: Field-level alignments and conflict notes for interchange.

findings.name: XBRL GL, ISO 20022 and adjacent mappings
findings.description: XBRL GL accountingEntries, documentInfo, entityInformation, entryHeader and entryDetail are the ledger-neutral interchange for journals. ISO 20022 bank-to-customer cash management (including BankToCustomerStatement camt.053) reports booked cash entries with bank transaction codes for sub-ledger reconciliation; those entries are single-sided servicer bookings, not balanced journals. FIBO BP transaction workflows align only as originating market events. Tax-audit export is supported by the XBRL GL TAF module developed with OECD SAF-T input; national SAF-T schemas are not claimed as fetched in this research.

questions.text: How is this journal projected to XBRL GL accountingEntries, entryHeader and entryDetail, including which modules (COR, BUS, MUC, USK, TAF, SRCD) are required?
How does a bank-to-customer statement entry map to a posting, including servicer reference, credit-debit indicator, booking and value times, and bank transaction code?
Which semantic conflicts (single-sided cash entry versus balanced journal, market transaction versus posting, recognition date versus booking date) are recorded for this instance?
Must this population be exported through XBRL GL TAF or a national tax-audit file, and which profile applies?

data_elements.name: Alignment conflict codes
data_elements.description: Recorded conflicts between this model and an aligned standard for the instance.

artifacts.name: XBRL GL instance
artifacts.description: Interchange instance of accountingEntries for one or more journals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by instance identifier plus reporting-entity and entriesType; not by creation date alone.

artifacts.name: Bank-to-customer statement
artifacts.description: ISO 20022 cash-management statement or notification carrying booked entries to be reconciled.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identify by message identifier and account-servicer statement identifier.

functions.name: Post balanced journal entry
functions.description: Validate identity, period openness, authorization and debit-credit equality, then post the header and lines so account balances change and the record becomes immutable.
preconditions: Every line references a known account
Debit total equals credit total in the balancing currency
Target period is open or an exception grant exists
Authorization and segregation-of-duties rules are satisfied
Master-system identifier is assigned or assignable
effects: Creates an immutable posted journal in the system of record

functions.name: Validate debit-credit balance
functions.description: Compute debit and credit totals in the balancing currency and accept or reject the header as a posting unit.
preconditions: Lines have debit-credit codes and unsigned amounts
Balancing currency is an ISO 4217 code
effects: Returns a validation result used as a posting gate

functions.name: Authorize journal entry
functions.description: Record the authorizer distinct from the initiator and attach the authorization event required before posting.
preconditions: Entry exists in a pre-posted state
Authorizer is permitted for the book and amount
effects: May block posting if segregation of duties fails

functions.name: Reverse or correct posted entry
functions.description: Create a new reversing or correcting journal linked to the original instead of updating posted amounts in place.
effects: Leaves the original posted record intact
Restores or adjusts account balances by the reversing amounts

functions.name: Reject or exception-post to closed period
functions.description: Block posting to a closed period unless a documented exception grant exists for adjusting entries.
preconditions: Period status is known for the book
effects: Records exception use when a grant is consumed

functions.name: Examine journal population for completeness and fraud characteristics
functions.description: Assemble the complete journal population, test accuracy and completeness, and select entries matching fraud-oriented criteria including automated items.
preconditions: Extract claims to be the full population
Control totals from the ledger are available

functions.name: Classify and reconcile a bank-booked entry
functions.description: Apply an ISO 20022 bank transaction code to a servicer-booked cash entry so it can be routed to the correct sub-ledger counterpart journal.
preconditions: Entry carries or can be assigned a bank transaction code
effects: Does not itself balance the books

functions.name: Export transactional ledger for audit or tax
functions.description: Project posted journals to XBRL GL, including TAF fields when required, while retaining drill-back to line detail.
effects: Produces an interchange artefact without deleting source journals

composition.purpose: Every posting line references the account whose balance it changes; the account master remains in the parent account model.
A payment may originate one or more postings, but many journals have no payment origin; correlation uses governed payment identifiers when present.
Align header and line semantics to accountingEntries, entryHeader, entryDetail, debitCreditCode and modular COR BUS MUC USK TAF SRCD fields without treating XML as the model.
Align servicer-booked cash entries, booking and value times, credit-debit indicators and bank transaction codes used to reconcile cash movements to sub-ledgers.

composition.target: IFRS Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
composition.purpose: Align recognition, derecognition, measurement bases, reporting period and qualitative characteristics that justify posting an element.
Express every monetary amount in a governed currency code with known minor units.
Record an adjacent meaning of financial transaction (market process flow) so it is not collapsed into a ledger posting.
Name the reporting entity that owns the books; party master data remains outside this model.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the posting ledger or account-servicer system of record and its identifier scheme
Bind every posting line to WM-ECO-015 account identifiers and a named book
Publish identity priority, RFC 3339 timestamp policy and posted-immutability rules in AGENTS.md
Name the reporting entity, functional currency and fiscal calendar that consume the postings
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint Dimension IRIs under the adopting package for WM-ECO-016 using the master-system journal identifier when it is unique; otherwise mint a UUID or ULID. Never use a posting date, period code or amount as an identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Prefer debit-credit code plus unsigned amount; do not mix signed amounts with a debit-credit code on the same line
Canonical currency is ISO 4217 alphabetic; retain numeric code only as a secondary label
Canonical timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Header identity is the master-system journal number qualified by entity and book
Line identity is parent journal identifier plus stable line number or line UUID
patch_rules: Posted amounts, accounts and debit-credit codes must not be patched in place
Corrections are new reversing or correcting journals that reference the original
Draft or parked entries may be patched until posted
Provenance and authorization events are append-only
compatibility_rules: New optional fields may be added; required balancing and identity fields must not be removed
ISO 20022 single-sided entries remain representable without forcing a false balanced header
XBRL GL module additions must not change the meaning of existing COR header and line fields

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the posting ledger or account servicer (journal entry number, accounting document number, or ISO 20022 AccountServicerReference)
Governed global identifier or IRI used for end-to-end payment or statement correlation when one exists
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or governed global identifier is available
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record every timestamp in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Distinguish accounting event time (document, posting, value or booking time) from observation or ingestion time when those differ, and persist both.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts such as journal vouchers use the ledger document number within entity and book; serial names must not embed a date as the identifying token.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Posted journals carry a content hash or control total; exports and population extracts must reproduce those totals, and silent rewrite of posted bytes is a control failure.

policies: Posted journal entries are immutable; corrections use reversing or restating entries
Debit totals must equal credit totals in the balancing currency before a header may post as a journal
Default access is deny; create and authorize are separate roles; read of personal-data lines is additionally restricted
Closed-period posting is forbidden without an explicit exception grant
Journal populations used for audit or tax export must be tested for completeness before sampling or filing

read: Permitted for roles with book-level or engagement-level scope
Personal-data lines require a tighter scope than header metadata
Auditors may read population extracts after completeness controls are applied
create: Allowed only through post or park functions with balance, period and authorization gates
Master-system identifier is assigned at create of the voucher, not inferred from the date
Bank-statement imports create candidate entries that still require counterpart balancing before they are journals
update: Posted records cannot be updated in place
Draft, parked or rejected entries may be updated until posted
State transitions append history rather than overwriting prior states
delete: Physical delete of posted entries is forbidden
Draft entries may be discarded before post
Disposal after retention expiry is a governed process and is blocked by legal hold

roles.name: Journal preparer
responsibilities: Submit for authorization without self-approval where dual control applies

roles.name: Posting authorizer
responsibilities: Approve closed-period exception requests within delegated limits

roles.name: Ledger controller
responsibilities: Own the chart-of-accounts binding to WM-ECO-015

roles.name: External auditor
responsibilities: Test completeness of the journal population
Inspect supporting evidence rather than relying on inquiry alone

roles.name: Dimension data steward
responsibilities: Maintain mappings to XBRL GL and ISO 20022

roles.name: Tax or regulatory examiner
responsibilities: Consume TAF or other audit-file exports
Request lineage from summary reports back to posting lines

access.default_rule: Deny create, update and delete of journals except to assigned preparer, authorizer and controller roles; deny read of personal-data lines except to roles with an explicit privacy scope.
exceptions: Break-glass read for a named incident with time-bounded grant and full audit log
Closed-period posting by a named controller with an exception grant
Auditor read of the full population extract for a scoped engagement
audit_requirements: Log initiator, authorizer, poster, timestamps, source system and control totals for every posted entry
Retain completeness tests of journal populations used in audits
Record overrides, exclusions from fraud-criteria testing, and legal holds

read_order: policies for posted immutability and period lock

coverage.claim: This structure covers the defensible operating surface of a recorded journal entry and atomic posting—identity, composition, balancing, measurement, recognition, control lifecycle, time, provenance, evidence, retention and interchange—aligned to XBRL GL, ISO 20022 cash reporting, ISO 4217, the IFRS Conceptual Framework and PCAOB journal-entry standards, without claiming universal completeness across all ledgers, jurisdictions or market-side transaction ontologies.

checklist.notes: Master-system journal or servicer reference first, then governed correlation identifiers, then Dimension UUID or ULID; dates excluded as identifiers.
Draft, posted, reversed, restated, auto-reversing, top-side and closed-period exception states with immutability of posted records.
References to accounts, payments, source documents, reporting entity, books and original entries being reversed.
Document, posting, value, booking and ingestion times; fiscal period assignment and cutoff.
Source system lineage, transformations, hashes or control totals, and actor history.
Reporting entity owns the books; ledger operator or account servicer maintains the record; book-level ownership of parallel GAAP views.
Debit-equals-credit gate, period-open gate, population completeness tests and cutoff checks.
Default deny, segregation of duties, privacy on personal-data lines, break-glass and auditor exceptions.
Posted physical delete forbidden; retention and legal hold; draft discard; tax-audit export via TAF alignment.
XBRL GL modules, ISO 20022 cash reporting and bank transaction codes, ISO 4217, IFRS recognition, FIBO conflict note.
Header-level debit and credit totals in a balancing currency, with explicit handling of single-sided bank entries.
PCAOB characteristics of fraudulent or unusual entries, management override, manual versus automated origin, and exclusion rationales.
ISO 4217 amounts, functional versus transaction currency, FX rate evidence and revaluation class.
Fiscal period binding, going-concern period context, late and post-close flags.
Books jurisdiction and tax-authority context for the reporting entity; posting itself is not a geospatial feature.

known_omissions: Official OECD SAF-T 2.0 XML schema was not retrieved in this run; TAF alignment is taken from XBRL GL's stated OECD tax-audit input, not from a national SAF-T implementation.
ISO 20022 camt.053 XSD field inventory was not downloaded; cash-entry alignment uses the MDR, catalogue and bank-transaction-code documents.
AAOIFI Islamic accounting, IPSAS public-sector budget accounting and Chinese Accounting Standards posting rules are not modelled.
Distributed-ledger, hash-chained or token-settlement journals lack primary support here and are gaps.

Payroll statutory postings, lease IFRS 16 mechanics, IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss engines and IFRS 15 contract-asset engines are consumers that generate journals, not part of this atomic posting model.
UETR and LEI are correlation or party identifiers only; party and payment masters remain sibling models.
conflicts: ISO 20022 bank-to-customer entries are single-sided booked cash movements; a double-entry journal is a balanced multi-account event. Mapping is reconciliation, not identity.
FIBO BP uses transaction for securities and derivatives process flows; that is not a ledger journal.
IFRS recognition date and measurement basis may differ from bank booking date and cash amount.
XBRL GL debitCreditCode with unsigned amount conflicts with signed-amount ledgers; canonical form prefers the code plus unsigned amount.

PCAOB notes that consolidating, combination and reclassification adjustments may not appear as formal general-ledger journal entries; those top-side items are in scope as exceptions, not as proof that every adjustment is a GL voucher.
The IFRS Conceptual Framework is not itself a Standard and does not override a specific IFRS that conflicts with it.
regional_assumptions: PCAOB AS 2201 and AS 2401 bind US issuer audits and are treated as highly informative controls for any Dimension, not as worldwide law.
IFRS Conceptual Framework 2018 is the recognition vocabulary used here; US GAAP, IPSAS and national GAAPs may assign different elements or timing.
XBRL GL USK module reflects Saxonic (US, UK, Australia, Canada and similar) journal-tagging needs and is optional.
ISO 20022 cash-reporting adoption and bank-transaction-code use vary by payment community (for example CGI, CBPR+, HVPS+) and must be recorded per servicer.
Retention periods are jurisdiction-specific and are not given a single number in this model.
adversarial_checks: A payment instruction is not a journal entry; treating WM-ECO-009 as this model would duplicate the payment sibling and break balancing semantics.
A bank statement Ntry can net many underlying customer transactions; assuming one Ntry equals one economic event is a false completeness claim.
Posted in-place edit would destroy the audit trail required by PCAOB journal-entry testing; any design that updates posted amounts fails the immutability policy.
Using posting date as the identifier collides restatements, multi-book copies and same-day batches.
Excluding automated journal entries from fraud testing contradicts PCAOB staff guidance that override risk is not limited to manual entries.
Claiming ISO 20022 or IFRS conformance for a Dimension instance is unwarranted unless the specific message version and recognition policy are evidenced.
